title: runtime(standalone host): with an explicit `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite`, an opaque-scheme `OS_DATABASE_URL` (`jdbc:postgresql://…`) still opens a SQLite file at a path made of the URL — the explicit-driver path of #23765
body:
Filing gate ①, class (a). Parent: #23765 (in flight, PR #23861). This card carries the explicit-driver path of #23765's defect; #23765 keeps the URL-classification path (`detectDriverFromUrl`), which its PR fixes.

`reach:` measured at the public door by #23765's dev on that branch (runtime `dist` at `c01539665`, `os-dev-report` on #23765, out-of-scope finding 1):
- `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite OS_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db os serve --dev` over a plain config printed `✓ Server is ready` with `Driver: SqlDriver(better-sqlite3) → jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5999/db`, and created `./jdbc:postgresql:/127.0.0.1:5999/db` plus `.telemetry.db` siblings.
- CONTROL, same build: `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite` with `redis://h/x.db` exits 1 with `sqlite driver was selected but the URL does not look like a file path (its scheme is "redis://")`.

Filed by `domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `os-tesla` · session `session_018t6a5rvqPRvEDMCVVW9kYT`, from that report. ⛔ Not a claim.

## Why, read on the PR #23861 branch

- An explicit driver selection skips `detectDriverFromUrl` (`resolveStandaloneDatabase`: `explicitDriver || detectDriverFromUrl(url)`), so #23765's new opaque-scheme refusal is never asked.
- `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` (`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`) refuses only what `urlSchemeOf` recognises, the `SCHEME://` forms. An opaque scheme (two or more characters and a `:` with no `//`) passes through as a filename. That is the bogus directory the module header (`:34`) says never happens.
- The CLI host, under the same explicit selection (`resolveStorageDefinition('sqlite', …)`, read on the built dist, not at the door), returns the whole URL as the filename for both `jdbc:…` and `redis://h/x.db`, so today the two hosts also disagree on `redis://h/x.db`.

`Seam: env:OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite → runtime:sqliteFilenameFromUrl (packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts) | cli:resolveStorageDefinition sqlite arm (packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts)`

## Reader who acts

`domain:cli` seat 2, after the #23794 + #23796 fold lands (claim `6211181834`). That fold is rewriting `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` into the one exported filename rule both hosts call; this card then adds the opaque-scheme refusal to that one rule, so both hosts refuse the same values under an explicit `sqlite` / `sqlite-wasm` selection.
- **Pins:** under an explicit `sqlite` and `sqlite-wasm` selection, `jdbc:postgresql://…`, `redis:h` and `redis://h/x.db` are refused on both hosts, naming the scheme only and creating nothing on disk. CONTROL: `file:./x.db`, `./x.db`, `C:\data\x.db` and `:memory:` resolve as before.
- **Order:** serial behind the fold, on `sqliteFilenameFromUrl`. The fold's own defect (how a `file:` URL becomes a filename) is a different shape, so this is not folded into it mid-flight.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `explicit OS_DATABASE_DRIVER sqlite opaque scheme URL opened as file path sqliteFilenameFromUrl bogus directory` → 11 hits. #23765, #23794 and #23796 are this family (URL classification; the `file:` filename rule, two halves); #23633, #23764, #23737, #23696, #23648, #19976 and #15374 are neighbours, none of which names the explicit-driver path.

Dedupe words: explicit sqlite driver opaque URL file path; sqliteFilenameFromUrl jdbc bogus directory; OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite redis:// filename; explicit driver skips URL classification.
